blocks.text: Chilliwack 55+ and 45+ age-restricted townhomes Market Guide

parts.t: This page shows every active MLS® listing for 55+ and 45+ age-restricted townhomes in Chilliwack, BC. Here is how the local sub-areas compare.
Sardis East Vedder
Sardis East Vedder: established family streets east of Vedder Road close to shops, parks and Sardis Secondary.
Sardis West Vedder
Sardis West Vedder: quiet cul-de-sacs and gated adult complexes west of Vedder Road near the Vedder River trails.
Vedder Crossing
Vedder Crossing: the commercial heart of the south side, with condos and townhomes close to the Vedder River.
Chilliwack Proper East
Chilliwack Proper East: central Chilliwack neighbourhoods with older detached homes, duplexes and infill townhomes.
Sardis South
Sardis South: newer subdivisions and townhome sites toward the Vedder River and Cultus Lake Road.
Garrison Crossing
Garrison Crossing: the former CFB Chilliwack base, now a walkable village of heritage-style homes, townhomes and condos.

Under the BC Strata Property Act, 55+ and 45+ age-restricted townhomes are strata-titled. Before removing subjects, ask for Form B, the strata minutes from the last two years, the depreciation report and the bylaws covering rentals, pets and age restrictions. In 55+ and 45+ complexes the age bylaws apply to at least one occupant, and they are enforced.

Floodplain: lower Sardis, Yarrow, Rosedale, Greendale and Fairfield Island all have parts in the Fraser and Vedder River floodplain, which the City's dike network protects. Get the property's flood construction level, find out the lender and insurer requirements, and look on title for a registered geotechnical or floodplain covenant.

Schools and transit: School District 33 (SD33) serves Chilliwack, with Sardis Secondary, G.W. Graham Middle-Secondary and Chilliwack Secondary, plus elementary catchments such as Unsworth, Watson and Vedder. Check the catchment with SD33 before you buy. Local BC Transit routes in Chilliwack run on Vedder Road, Luckakuck Way and Young Road, while Route 66, the Fraser Valley Express, connects Chilliwack with Abbotsford and with Carvolth Exchange in Langley.

Where are 55+ and 45+ age-restricted townhomes for sale in Chilliwack usually located?

Most 55+ and 45+ age-restricted townhomes in Chilliwack come up in Sardis East Vedder, Sardis West Vedder, Vedder Crossing, Chilliwack Proper East, Sardis South and Garrison Crossing. Each area has its own mix of age, lot size and price, so I recommend shortlisting two or three neighbourhoods before you book showings.
How often do these Chilliwack 55+ townhome listings update?
The MLS® feed from the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board refreshes this page several times a day, which means new listings, price changes and sold statuses show up fast.
What should I check on zoning, strata or ALR before buying a Chilliwack 55+ townhome?

Age-restricted 55+ and 45+ townhomes are strata-titled, which falls under the BC Strata Property Act. Before you remove subjects, get Form B, the depreciation report, the bylaws on rentals, pets and age restrictions, and strata minutes going back two years. Complexes that are 55+ and 45+ enforce their age bylaws, and those bylaws cover at least one occupant.
Are any Chilliwack 55+ and 45+ age-restricted townhomes in the floodplain?

Flood risk: some of Yarrow, Greendale, Fairfield Island, Rosedale and lower Sardis is in the Fraser and Vedder River floodplain, with the City's dike network protecting it. Ask what the property's flood construction level is, what lender and insurer requirements apply, and whether title carries a geotechnical or floodplain covenant.
Which schools serve Chilliwack 55+ and 45+ age-restricted townhomes?

School District 33 (SD33) covers Chilliwack. Sardis and the south side go on to Sardis Secondary and G.W. Graham, and the north side goes to Chilliwack Secondary. Because catchments change, check with SD33 about a specific address.
Is public transit available near Chilliwack 55+ and 45+ age-restricted townhomes?

Yes. Local Chilliwack routes from BC Transit use Young Road, Luckakuck Way and Vedder Road, and the Fraser Valley Express links up with Abbotsford and Langley. Bus service is thin or absent in rural areas like Ryder Lake, Greendale and Columbia Valley.
